policy: A record may only promote a service to RUNTIME_VERIFIED when all four stages are true. The generator refuses to consume a record whose handlerId or nativeCommand disagrees with the active catalog or the native command registry, so a stale or edited record fails services:check instead of silently promoting a service.

method.chain: React control click -> OperationService.executeCapability -> NativeClient.executeCapability -> resolveNativeCommand allowlist -> Tauri invoke -> registered #[tauri::command] -> native Rust -> real Windows API, registry read, file read or child process -> OperationResult returned over IPC -> React state -> rendered DOM text
method.evidenceRule: renderedEvidence is copied from document.body.innerText of the running application after the operation completed, so it is what a user actually saw and not a re-derivation from source.

records.renderedEvidence: Before the fix: status failed, errorCode essential_catalog_unreadable, summary The bundled recommendation catalog could not be read. After the fix: status completed, errorCode null, summary The recommendation catalog was resolved against the measured Windows uninstall registry. Policy revision 2026.09.26. Policy digest c2bbac914bd5058e. Installed here 1 / 1. Package checks passed: not requested. Table row: Google Chrome.
records.interpretation: This service had never worked on any machine. RawCatalog and RawCatalogItem declared snake_case field names while resources/essential-software.json writes camelCase, so serde_json failed on the first field and load_catalog returned essential_catalog_unreadable. The existing test only parsed the resource into a serde_json::Value, which proved the file was well formed but never proved the typed struct matched it, and include_str! guaranteed the bytes were present. Two tests now perform the real deserialisation. Package checks are reported as not requested because no winget lookup was asked for, so no package identifier is claimed as verified.

records.interpretation: This is the two-providers-disagree case working as designed. The file walk measures 0 B and 0 files because neither root exists on this machine, while the Delivery Optimization cmdlet reports 2.0 GB. Both readings are shown and neither is reconciled into a single number, so a user cannot mistake one provider's answer for the machine's real cache size. A missing root is reported as root_does_not_exist rather than as an empty cache.

records.renderedEvidence: These files were not modified since 180 days ago. This machine does not reliably keep last-access timestamps, so "old" here does not mean "unused". This service is read-only. It never deletes, moves, or quarantines anything. Access time is system-managed, it is not applied to files. Windows reports disablelastaccess = 2, so last-access timestamps are not a reliable last-used signal. Rows fall back to modification time and are described as "not modified since". Measured from: fsutil, value as Windows reported it: 2.
records.interpretation: The last-access policy is measured from fsutil and reported before the result, and the service refuses to call a file 'unused' when the machine does not track access time. The wording is 'not modified since', never 'not used since'. This is the exact distinction the module doc was written for, and it holds at runtime.
